title: Generic algebraicity gives quasi-finiteness over a point of local dimension at most one
statement: Let $g:Z\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $s\in S$. Suppose that $\mathcal O_{S,s}$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and has Krull dimension at most $1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Suppose that for every generic point $\eta$ of every irreducible component of $Z$ [def-sc-generic-point, def-weil-irreducible-components], the induced extension $\kappa(g(\eta))\subseteq\kappa(\eta)$ of residue fields [def-weil-residue-field] is algebraic, meaning that every element satisfies a nonzero polynomial over $\kappa(g(\eta))$. Then $g$ is quasi-finite at every $z\in Z$ with $g(z)=s$, in the sense of [pqf-def-quasifinite]. No properness, normality, or global Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0AB6, varieties-lemma-quasi-finite-in-codim-1, condition (1); statement at label lemma-quasi-finite-in-codim-1

proof.text: Fix $z\in Z$ over $s$. Choose an affine neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $s$, with corresponding prime $\mathfrak p$, and an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ containing $z$ and contained in $g^{-1}(V)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], $A$ is a finite type $R$-algebra. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], $B=R_{\mathfrak p}\cong\mathcal O_{S,s}$. Thus $B$ is Noetherian and local, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pB$ and $\dim B\le1$. Write $k=B/\mathfrak m=\kappa(s)$ and $M=R\setminus\mathfrak p$.

Put $C=A\otimes_R B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $\operatorname{Spec}C$ is the base change of $U\to V$ to $\operatorname{Spec}B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change], $A\to C$ is localization at the image of $M$. If $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ generate $A$ over $R$, then $a_i\otimes1$ generate $C$ over $B$: every pure tensor is a $B$-multiple of a polynomial in these elements, and every tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors. Thus $C$ is of finite type over $B$ in [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra].

A minimal prime $Q$ of $A$ gives a generic point $\eta_Q$ of the irreducible component $V(Q)\subset U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes]. Its closure in $Z$ is an irreducible component of $Z$: if that closure is contained in an irreducible closed subset $H\subset Z$, then $H\cap U$ is an irreducible closed subset of $U$ containing $V(Q)$, hence equals $V(Q)$ by maximality; the nonempty open $H\cap U$ is dense in $H$, so $H=\overline{V(Q)}$. This is precisely the maximality in [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Since $\overline{\{\eta_Q\}}=\overline{V(Q)}$, $\eta_Q$ is the generic point of this component as in [def-sc-generic-point]. The assumed generic algebraicity therefore says $\kappa(Q)/\kappa(Q\cap R)$ is algebraic. Here the residue fields are the same in the open subschemes and their ambient schemes by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization].

Let $Q'$ be any minimal prime of $C$ and $Q_0=Q'\cap A$. By [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes], $Q_0$ contains a minimal prime $Q$ of $A$. Since $Q_0$ avoids the image of $M$, so does $Q$. By (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso], $QC$ is a prime contained in $Q'$; minimality gives $QC=Q'$ and then $Q=Q_0$. Put $q_0=Q\cap R$ and $q=Q'\cap B$. The same prime correspondence for $R\to B$ gives $q=q_0B$, with $q_0\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Clause (3) of that node identifies $\kappa(Q)\cong\kappa(Q')$ and $\kappa(q_0)\cong\kappa(q)$ compatibly with their structure maps. Hence Step 3 implies that $\kappa(Q')/\kappa(q)$ is algebraic. This verifies the generic hypothesis after localization without assuming $Z$ or $S$ globally Noetherian.

Let $P\subset C$ be any prime above $\mathfrak m$. Choose a minimal prime $Q'\subseteq P$, again using [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes]. Set $q=Q'\cap B$, $E=B/q$, $D=C/Q'$, and $r=P/Q'\subset D$. Then $E\hookrightarrow D$ is an inclusion of domains, $D$ is a finite type $E$-algebra (use the images of the generators of $C$), and $E$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], applied to the quotient $B\to B/q$, generated by zero extra elements. The prime $r$ contracts to $\mathfrak m/q$ in $E$. Step 4 says $\operatorname{Frac}(D)=\kappa(Q')$ is algebraic over $\operatorname{Frac}(E)=\kappa(q)$, so $\operatorname{trdeg}_E D=0$ by [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Also $\kappa(r)=\operatorname{Frac}(C/P)=\kappa(P)$ and $\kappa(\mathfrak m/q)=k$. Under [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-homeomorphism-zero-locus], chains of primes of $E$ lift to chains of primes of $B$ containing $q$; hence their lengths are at most one by [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

If $q=\mathfrak m$, then $E=k$ and $\operatorname{ht}_E(\mathfrak m/q)=0$. Apply [lem-trf-affine-dimension-inequality] to $E\hookrightarrow D$, $\mathfrak m/q$ and $r$, with all its hypotheses checked in Step 5. It gives $\operatorname{ht}_D(r)\le0-\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(P)$. Both height and transcendence degree are nonnegative, so $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(P)=0$. This is the vertical-component case, including the case $\dim B=0$.

source.place: Tag 0AB6, vertical-component case, written using the dimension inequality of Algebra Tag 02IJ

proof.text: If $q\ne\mathfrak m$, then $q\subsetneq\mathfrak m$. The strict chain $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak m/q$ in $E$ and the upper bound on chain lengths in Step 5 give $\operatorname{ht}_E(\mathfrak m/q)=1$. Moreover $r\ne(0)$, since otherwise $P=Q'$ would have contraction both $\mathfrak m$ and $q$. As $D$ is a domain, $(0)\subsetneq r$ gives $\operatorname{ht}_D(r)\ge1$. Apply [lem-trf-affine-dimension-inequality] to the same inclusion and primes as in Step 6. It yields $1\le\operatorname{ht}_D(r)\le1-\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(P)$, and hence $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(P)=0$. Thus Steps 6 and 7 cover every component through every closed-fibre point.

source.place: Tag 0AB6, horizontal-component dimension-formula argument; Algebra Tag 02IJ, inequality clause

proof.text: The closed fibre of $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is $Y=\operatorname{Spec}F$ with $F=C/\mathfrak mC$: tensoring $C$ with $k=B/\mathfrak m$ sends $c\otimes\bar b$ to $bc\bmod\mathfrak mC$, with inverse $\bar c\mapsto c\otimes1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-homeomorphism-zero-locus], its primes correspond to primes $P$ of $C$ over $\mathfrak m$, and its residue field at $P/\mathfrak mC$ is $\operatorname{Frac}(C/P)$. The images of the finite algebra generators of $C$ generate $F$ over $k$, so $Y$ is of finite type over the field $k$ by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Steps 6 and 7 show that every point of $Y$ has residue transcendence degree zero over $k$. Apply part (a) of [lem-kun-closed-point-field]: every point of $Y$ is closed.

Since all primes of $F$ are maximal, there is no strict inclusion between distinct primes. By [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], $\dim F\le0$, equivalently $\dim Y\le0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-dim-zero-artinian] to the finite type $k$-scheme $Y$: its underlying space is finite and discrete. This also includes $F=0$, when the fibre is empty.

The fibre $U_s$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_R k)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. The $B$-algebra $C=A\otimes_R B$ therefore has $C\otimes_B k\cong A\otimes_R k$, explicitly $(a\otimes b)\otimes c\mapsto a\otimes bc$, with inverse $a\otimes c\mapsto(a\otimes1)\otimes c$. Thus $U_s\cong Y$, and the set of points of $U$ mapping to $s$ is finite by the fibre homeomorphism in [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Apply [pqf-lem-locqf-fibre-discrete] to $U\to V$. It is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], used in both directions: an affine open $U'\subseteq U$ and an affine open $V'\subseteq V$ with $g(U')\subseteq V'$ are affine opens of $Z$ and $S$, so $\mathcal O_S(V')\to\mathcal O_Z(U')$ is of finite type because $g$ is locally of finite type. It is quasi-finite at $z$. The affine neighbourhoods witnessing this for $U\to V$ are also affine open neighbourhoods in $Z$ and $S$, so they witness quasi-finiteness of $g$ at $z$ by [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Since $z$ was arbitrary over $s$, this proves the item.
